title: How to change cursor in Safari on Mac: complete guide for system pointer settings
metaTitle: How to change cursor on Mac: Safari and System Settings
description: Learn how to change cursor on Mac. While Safari has no individual setting, you can adjust your system-wide pointer size and color in macOS Accessibility.
targetKeyword: how to change cursor on mac
intro: To change the cursor on a Mac, you must adjust your system-wide macOS settings, as Safari does not provide a browser-specific option for this. Any changes to the pointer size or color will apply across all applications on your computer, including Safari.
tldr: Open System Settings on your Mac.
Navigate to Accessibility and select Display.
Adjust the Pointer size and colors in the Pointer section.
Note that these changes affect your entire system, not just Safari.

blocks.text: Why you cannot change the cursor in Safari alone

Many users search for a way to change their cursor specifically within the Safari browser. It is important to understand that macOS handles the mouse pointer at the system level. Safari, like most other applications on your Mac, simply inherits the pointer appearance defined in your System Settings. There is no hidden menu or setting inside Safari to swap your arrow for a different icon or to change its color independently.

Because the cursor is a primary tool used thousands of times daily, Apple keeps its behavior consistent across the interface. This ensures that you do not lose track of your pointer when moving between different apps. If you want to change how it looks, you must do so for the entire operating system.
How to change cursor on Mac via System Settings

If you are using a modern version of macOS, such as Sonoma or Sequoia, you have significant control over the appearance of your pointer. You can make it larger, change its fill color, or alter the outline color to make it stand out against complex web pages.

items: Click the Apple Menu in the top-left corner and choose System Settings.
In the left sidebar, click on Accessibility.
Select Display from the list of options.
Scroll down until you reach the Pointer section.
Use the Pointer size slider to make your cursor easier to see.
Click the color wells for Pointer outline color or Pointer fill color to customize your look.

blocks.text: Once you make these changes, they take effect immediately. You will see the new cursor style in Safari right away. If you ever feel like the custom colors are distracting, you can return to this menu and click the Reset button to restore the default black and white pointer.
What to do if your cursor disappears in Safari

Sometimes the cursor might seem to vanish or stop changing shape when you hover over links. This is usually a temporary rendering issue rather than a settings problem. The first step is to move your mouse quickly or shake your finger on the trackpad. macOS has a built-in feature that enlarges the pointer when it detects rapid movement, helping you find it quickly on a busy screen.

If the cursor fails to change from an arrow to a hand when hovering over a link, try refreshing the specific web page. If that does not work, quit Safari completely by pressing Command + Q and relaunching it. This clears out temporary states that might be causing the browser to misinterpret your mouse position.
Can you use custom cursor shapes?

macOS does not natively support changing the cursor into custom shapes, like animated characters or unique icons. While you can change the size and color, the basic arrow and hand shapes remain standard. Some users experiment with third-party software to attempt this, but these tools can be unstable.

If you decide to try third-party cursor tools, be aware of security warnings. macOS may block these apps from modifying system files. If you see an untrusted source error, you must go to System Settings > Privacy & Security and manually allow the application to run. Always verify that such software is reputable before granting it deep system access.

faq.question: Does Safari have a setting to change the mouse pointer?
faq.answer: No. Safari does not have an individual setting for the cursor. You must change it through the macOS System Settings, which applies the change globally.

faq.question: Will my cursor change in other apps if I change it for Safari?
faq.answer: Yes. Because the cursor is controlled at the system level, any changes you make to its size or color will be reflected in all applications, including Safari, Chrome, and your desktop.

faq.question: How do I make my cursor easier to find?
faq.answer: Go to System Settings > Accessibility > Display. You can increase the pointer size using the slider or enable the shake-to-locate feature, which enlarges the pointer when you move it quickly.

steps.name: Open System Settings
steps.text: Click the Apple menu () in the top-left corner of your screen and select System Settings.

steps.name: Navigate to Accessibility
steps.text: Click on Accessibility in the left-hand sidebar.

steps.name: Access Display settings
steps.text: Find the Vision section and click on Display.

steps.name: Adjust Pointer settings
steps.text: Scroll down to the Pointer section. Use the slider to change the size, or click the color wells to change the fill and outline colors of your cursor.

troubleshooting.problem: Cursor does not change to hand on links
troubleshooting.fix: Refresh the page or quit and restart Safari.

troubleshooting.problem: Custom cursor app is blocked by system
troubleshooting.fix: Go to System Settings > Privacy & Security and click Allow next to the blocked app.
